120	Now, after we have seen the Torah and the verse
121	in the Writings, in the book of Kohelet, let's look at the Mishnah
122	in tractate Bava
123	Metsia, chapter 4 of Bava Metsia, where it is written as follows:
124	If he drew the fruit but did not give him the money, he cannot
125	retract. If he gave him the money but did not draw the fruit,
126	he can retract. But they said: He who punished the people of the generation
127	of the Flood and of the generation of the Dispersion will, in the future, exact payment from
128	whoever does not stand by his word. Let's try to understand this for a moment.
129	First of all, let's study only the topic there in tractate Bava
130	Metsia.
131	Tractate Bava Metsia is the middle tractate between
132	two other tractates, Bava Kamma and Bava Batra. These three
133	tractates, Bava Kamma, Bava Metsia and Bava Batra,
134	make up a larger tractate called Nezikin,
135	which deals, in essence, and it is found in the order of
136	Nezikin, among the six orders of the Mishnah in the Talmud,
137	and these tractates deal with matters of
138	monetary law. In chapter 4 of Bava Metsia the subject is
139	the system of acquisitions, how one acquires things. That is, there are
140	objects that are mine, property that is mine,
141	and the question is how an asset becomes mine or
142	leaves my possession. Now, here we are speaking of two
143	people in the discussion here
144	in the Mishnah,
145	where one sells fruit to another,
146	say a greengrocer or a fruit seller
147	in the market, of course, and now
148	buyers come, a customer comes and wants to buy. So one must know that
149	when buying fruit, the acquisition is not made by paying
150	money, as is commonly thought today, but rather
151	the acquisition is made by means of
152	drawing, that is, from the moment the buyer drew the thing
153	that he is buying, in this case fruit, kind of, from
154	the seller's possession, he drew it, that is, he joined it to himself,
155	that is what creates the acquisition, even if he has not yet
156	paid the
157	money. Let me give an example, imagine a person
158	who goes into a shop, not one that sells fruit and vegetables,
159	but he goes to buy a vase or some
160	glassware, right? So there is the display
161	in the shop and he says to the seller: I want
162	the third vase there on the second shelf on the
163	right. The seller goes and takes
164	it down,
165	and this vase falls
166	and breaks. Even if he paid the
167	money, the customer, as if, he still just needs to be brought
168	it. The payment of the money does not make the acquisition until
169	the vase actually comes into his possession, that is, what
170	makes the acquisition here is
171	the drawing. Now, after more or less this principle,
172	let's look again at the Mishnah: If he drew the
173	fruit but did not give him
174	the money. They agreed that he buys from him, I don't know how many,
175	ten crates of oranges or apples, I don't know
176	what, and he drew, the customer drew the fruit from the
177	owner of the shop, and has not yet given him the fruit, has not given
178	him the money, he has not yet paid him, he only
179	drew and did not pay the money, and afterwards he wants
180	to retract, he says, you know what, no, I don't
181	want the fruit, it is not good, I am not buying it. But he already drew it. The shop owner can say to
182	him:
183	Sorry, you drew it, it is already yours, I am not willing to take
184	it back. That is the meaning of: If he drew fruit from him and did not
185	give him the money, he cannot retract. If he gave him
186	the money but did not draw fruit from him, that is, they
187	agreed that he buys these crates of oranges
188	and he already paid him the money but still did not
189	draw it, he can retract,
190	because there was no acquisition here. What is the determining acquisition?
191	It is the acquisition by drawing. Now, what happens here? To this
192	the Mishnah refers and says: But they said: He who punished
193	the people of the generation of the Flood and of the generation of the Dispersion will, in the future, exact payment
194	from whoever does not stand by his word. That is,
195	you committed yourself, true, you have not yet carried out the acquisition, but
196	you committed yourself. So by strict law you can retract,
197	but know that this is a grave matter, what is written here: He who
198	punished the people of the generation of the Flood and of the generation of the Dispersion will
199	in the future exact payment from whoever does not stand by his word. The generation of
200	the Flood is the story that appears at the end of the book, at the end of
201	Parashat Bereshit, the beginning of Parashat Noach, right: All flesh had
202	corrupted its way upon the earth, and I am about to destroy them from the earth,
203	and the Flood came
204	and essentially destroyed all
205	living things. The people of the generation of the Flood were wicked people,
206	and the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed them. Ten generations
207	later they built the Tower of Babel, this is the generation of the Dispersion, in which
208	at first the whole earth was of one language and one speech,
209	and then the Holy One, blessed be He, confounded their language, and this is called
210	Dispersion, He divided
211	them. And this punishment of the generation of the Flood and of the generation of
212	the Dispersion is the punishment of a person who does not stand
213	by his word. And here note that the Mishnah is not speaking
214	of matters between man and the Almighty, it is speaking of matters between
215	man and his fellow, of a business
216	commitment, by word, by word. So true, apparently there
217	was no drawing here and therefore you cannot, the shop
218	owner cannot say to him, listen, you drew it, it is yours.
219	He can retract, but if he retracts
220	he is in effect breaking his word, breaking his promise.
221	Whoever breaks his promise, something very grave is written here,
222	that he is destined to end up like the people of the generation of the
223	Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion ended up, and one must know that these matters
224	are not trivial. One must understand what happened in the generation of the Flood and in the generation of the Dispersion that relates to the matter of
225	not
226	standing by one's word.
227	What all this shows us is that speech is something very, very
228	serious. We set out from this, remember this whole journey,
229	we set out from the verses in the Torah, the three verses in the Torah,
230	in the book of Devarim, in our parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzei: When
231	you make a vow to HaShem, do not delay in paying it, and so on.
232	We saw the verses also in Kohelet, we saw now
233	this Mishnah in tractate Bava Metsia, and now let's
234	try to go a bit deeper. Let's perhaps begin with the matter
235	of what is the connection between standing by one's word and the terrible punishment
236	that appears here, which is parallel to the generation of
237	the Flood and the generation of the
238	Dispersion. So for this purpose let's go to the book of Bereshit.
